speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned generalized fatigue, mild fever, abdominal pain, and nausea; to begin our assessment, have you experienced any recent changes in your bowel habits, such as diarrhea or constipation, or any blood in your stool?

speaker: Patient
text: 47-year-old female. The patient describes a 3-week history of generalized fatigue, mild fever, abdominal pain, and nausea. She recalls attending the state fair over a month ago where she tried various regional foods. Recently, she has observed the darkening of her urine, which she believes is due to inadequate water intake. She has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details. Given your history of type 2 diabetes, dark urine, and abdominal pain, could you please clarify if you have also experienced increased thirst, frequent urination, or any blurry vision? Additionally, have you noticed any yellowing of your skin or the whites of your eyes?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized fatigue and mild fever. I also have Abdominal pain, Nausea, Dark urine.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Viral Hepatitis.

The combination of a fairground food history, dark urine, nausea, fatigue, and abdominal pain strongly suggests liver involvement, likely from a viral etiology. I need to confirm if you have seen any yellowing in your eyes or skin and if you have had any contact with needles or unprotected sexual partners to rule out other causes.

REQUEST TEST: Liver Function Panel (AST, ALT, Bilirubin, Alkaline Phosphatase)
REQUEST TEST: Hepatitis Serology Panel (A, B, C)
REQUEST IMAGES: Right Upper Quadrant Ultrasound
